A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoDiscovery work and support comparison of text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. V3 retains the original scientific material, adds a Research Changelog, and removes the NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments across 21 datasets, human evaluations, discovery-agent validation, and additional analyses and experimental outputs in its appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds a belief-update diagnostic and sequential-versus-batched execution measurements in the Research Changelog.

M1.justification: The Research Changelog substantially revises the procedure: Boolean belief elicitation becomes five-category sampling with abstention and evidence weighting; normalized mean belief change and continuous rewards replace KL-based binary scoring; recursive UCB1 replaces progressive widening. Batched parallel expansion and automatic or researcher-provided warmstarts are also introduced. The original main-text method remains documented.

E1.justification: The original 21 datasets remain. Changelog Section 2.4 adds execution experiments on Swedish Melanoma and Breast Cancer datasets, while Section 1.1 adds a controlled health-and-lifespan scenario using balanced supporting and contradictory evidence.

E2.justification: The existing search and automatic-reward comparator sets are retained. The changelog adds evaluated comparisons between explicit Bayesian updating and implicit in-context updating, and between batched and sequential execution.

E3.justification: The original benchmark and human-study protocols remain unchanged. New protocols include a GPT-4o diagnostic with 25 supporting and 25 contradictory facts, and an o4-mini timing comparison using 100 sequential experiments versus 500 batched experiments with batch size five and five threads.

E4.justification: V3 adds a diagnostic testing whether implicit updating retains prior beliefs, a batching-efficiency comparison, and qualitative analysis of tree depth under recursive UCB1. The original reward comparisons, diversity analysis, belief-shift analysis, validation studies, and error examples are retained.

E5.justification: The existing confidence interval, 10,000-resample bootstrap procedure, agreement statistics, and uncertainty displays are retained. The changelog supplies no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance procedures. Changes to internal belief distributions concern the method rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original table values and plotted results are unchanged. New results include a prior belief of 0.96, implicit posterior of 0.51, and explicit posterior of 0.74. V3 also reports approximately eight hours for 100 sequential versus 500 batched o4-mini experiments, and qualitatively reports deeper trees and more complex hypotheses. These are additional findings under new conditions.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained Beta-belief, KL-surprise, and UCT definitions, the changelog introduces normalized mean belief change and derives its theoretical maximum as a function of prior parameters, evidence weight, and sample limit. The constrained optimization and clipped maximizer provide a substantive new mathematical basis for normalization, absent from v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and headline claims: Bayesian-surprise-guided open-ended discovery, progressive-widening MCTS, evaluation on 21 datasets, 5–29% more surprising discoveries, and approximately 67% alignment with human surprise.

C2.justification: The changelog substantially expands the interpretation of belief elicitation and search. It attributes prior neglect to instruction tuning, argues for categorical elicitation, distinguishes conflicting evidence from missing evidence, identifies configuration-dependent belief shifts, and criticizes information loss from binary rewards and shallow progressive-widening trees. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds categorical scores of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1, evidence-weight control, threaded batching without replacement, and a default of eight root warmstart expansions. Timing-study batch and thread counts are disclosed. Original agent prompts, configuration details, and the code link remain.

R1.justification: Five references are added: Brochu, Chaslot, Desautels, Frazier, and Scheffer and their respective coauthors. They connect the revisions to Bayesian-optimization warmstarts and batching, parallel MCTS, and belief inertia. The main positioning relative to autonomous-discovery research is unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and original appendix content are largely unchanged. V3 adds a dated Research Changelog and title-page pointer, renumbers appendix Sections 8–15 as 1–8, and removes the checklist. These are localized structural changes rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V3 adds the Algorithm 5 display and reflows surrounding material. Table 1 moves from page 7 to page 8, and Table 3 from page 8 to page 9. Existing figures and table contents remain unchanged, with no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful implementation information, a normalization derivation, and targeted empirical evidence. However, the substantial algorithm revisions lack corresponding comparative and human evaluations, and Changelog Section 1.2 does not justify its inference that independent Boolean sampling systematically overestimates belief. The added substance and new methodological concerns leave the net effect on paper quality uncertain.
